You receive a table, calculate a number and send a report. Next month, another
table arrives. Later, someone corrects an earlier delivery. These five lessons
show how to repeat the work and keep the original report explainable.

## Before you begin

You should be comfortable creating an R data frame and using a pipe. Familiarity
with `dplyr::mutate()` and `dplyr::summarise()` helps. You do not need a database,
dbt, pointblank or a data catalog to start.

```{r installation, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("JanWein/tidyweave")
```

Use R 4.2 or later. This installs the development version, whose API can still
change. Lessons 3 to 5 also use `install.packages("duckdb")` for local history.

## Follow the lessons in order

| Lesson | What you will be able to do | What you need |
|---|---|---|
| [1. Build a product](first-product.html) | Prepare a table and collect the result | R and tidyweave |
| [2. Check a delivery](check-delivery.html) | Find a bad row, correct it and try again | R and tidyweave |
| [3. Publish and correct data](publish-data.html) | Save a checked table while retaining earlier values | Optional DuckDB >= 1.5.5 |
| [4. Save a report](save-report.html) | Save agreed calculations and read them without recalculating | Optional DuckDB >= 1.5.5 |
| [5. Work through a reporting month](getting-started.html) | Handle complete monthly deliveries and a late correction | Optional DuckDB >= 1.5.5 |

Each lesson includes its own setup. Start a fresh R session and run its visible
code from top to bottom; objects from another lesson are not required. Examples
use synthetic data and temporary folders. Use a project folder for real work.

**[Begin lesson 1: Build a product](first-product.html)**

## After the basics

[Learn](learn.html) organizes the remaining guides by task. The
[function reference](../reference/index.html) lists arguments and return values.
[Terms](glossary.html) explains the small vocabulary as you encounter it.
If a call fails, use [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.html).

This learning structure follows the distinction between a guided
[tidymodels introduction](https://www.tidymodels.org/start/) and its
[task-focused learning articles](https://www.tidymodels.org/learn/).
